airy was happening and endeavored to
hold her still.


The spectators, too, helped, but Miss
Ehlers's shakes did not subside until the
band had turned another corner and the
music could no longer be heard. Then
she hurst into tears and calling a taxicab
hurried to her home.

Three Boy Scouts of Newark. Charles

But they were all together Saturday

mountain They were in Scout uniforms

ahead. Edward and Walker followed
and saw Charles run up an embank-
n.ont and suddenly disappear.


They ran forward and discovered that
they were on the edge of the Spottiswood
quarry. Below was a drop of 100 feet
and toward the base were jagged rocks
and deep holes.


The two boys could not see Charles
and began crying his name. Getting
no reply, Edward leaned far over and
scanned the quarry pit and gave cry
of fright.


There's Charley down there"
He had fallen down and lay face up.
Quickly the boys rushed down and found
their comrade bleeding and unconscious.
They summoned aid and Charles was
taken to Orange Memorial Hospital.
where he died. His head had been badly
crushed and his body badly broken.

est in the financial situation today
converged upon the movement of the
stock exchange. This was not be-
cause of anything important in the
outside news. What the market was
called upon to decide was whether

warrant some setback.


The answer was given with suffi-

eral way was that the forces making

The big st. Johns, which has been
making regular trips to Colonial

to the beach this morning, and with
the docking of the boat tonight the
summer season will be over. This
years Labor Day celebration was
one of the best in the steamers his
tory. Saturdays afternoon trip and
Sunday and Mondays runs carried

ence

meant as unerringly as though it were
aimed like a rifle.


In the present piece, for which the
stalwart honest figures OF Henry Wads-
worth Longfellow's poem was sufficient
starting point, we have the sacrificing,
gentle mother the tender, pretty daugh-
ter. the gallant. spirited son, the town
sossips and loafers the mean, vindictive
squire and his vicious son and, of
course, in the prologue the village school
and the boys i'll the old swimming hole.


The humor of the exaggerated coun-
try types in all this was generally crude,
the emotion often sentimental and the
action sometimes artificial, leading nat



stood daughter says please, please
father. don't look at me like that" But
1t all moved with such unfaltering and
at times practiced skill to its predes
tined end-the end. one might say, that
had been predetermined for it almost
from the first days of the movies.


The most effective scene perhaps
went to George Hackathorne as the
crippled young man who crawled to
avenge his sister. dragging his useless
legs after him through the mud and the
rain that came with the absolutely es-
sential rainstorm. Will Walling had
little to do. despite his titular role. but
look burly and periodically poke men in
the jaw with righteous wrath at a given
signal. Virginia Valli. Bessie Love.
FULLY Marshall and Eddie Gribbon also
stood out in their parts, and the ex-
cerpts from Longfellow's cherished
poem were for once handled with dis
erection, instead of being dragged through
the mire like the famed youth.

TOMS RIVER, n. j., Oct. 17.-Both

The 1922 bull market, according to
one keen market observer of the
swings over past years, has been made
up of minor upward movements, the
present movement having begun in
July. "The first swing" he says, "got
under way in August, 1921, with the
average price Of twenty industrials
around 70. From that point stocks
advanced consistently, with never more
than two-point reaction at the most,
until the first week in June this year,
when we ran into period Of enor-
nous volume with succession Of mil
lion share days. Stocks had gone up
an average of 20 points, and the first
distributing point was in order, prior
to summer dullness, which developed
during July. The decline in June
averaged seven points. The second up
ward movement then got going, and
present levels are approximately 10
points above the June lows and 80
points from the first starting point"

The President and Mrs. Harding

today and "all Washington" an.
parently turned out to wish then.
Happy New Year."


1t was the first time in nearly
ten years that the historic New
Year reception at the White House
has been held. and it had to be
divided into two sections-so great
was the number of people who
turned out to do honor to the CHIEF
Executive.


Officials in Morning.


In the morning the official world
was received, in the afternoon the
general public, the President and Mrs.
Harding retiring between one and
two o'clock to their private apart
ments for a rest and luncheon.


Coming from the North and South,
the East and West, the citizens Of
America flocked to the White House.
standing in line for hours before they
could gain entrance. Those who con
troll the destinies of the Republic were
present and those who pay the ex,
penses.


Every country of the world with
which the United States maintains
diplomatic relations was represented
by the entire embassy or legation
staff, and for the first time since the
great war set the world on fire, diplo-
mats from Germany and Austria
rubbed elbows with the representa-.
tives Of the nations who had been their
enemies.


Court dress, long packed away in
camphor, was brought out for the oc.
casion and the gold lace Of diplomatic
uniforms We'd in splendor with the
gold lace Of the full dress uniforms Of
the army, navy, and marine corps.


Promptly at II o'clock the front
doors Of the mansion Of the Chief
Executive were swung open. Visitors
Day was announced. A minute later
an army Of men, women, and children
wedged their way toward the entrance
Another minute and Americas big.
gest reception was under way.


With outstretched hands, the Pres
ident and Mrs. Harding welcomed the
first line of visitors.

first extended a greeting to the Vice
President and Mrs, Coolidge, the mem.
bers Of the Cabinet and their wives,
who were received in their private
apartments. They came down the
state stairway together, the Vice Presi.
dent and Mrs. Coolidge following the
President and Mrs. Harding, and Cabi.
net behind them two and two.

Fughes were followed closely by Mr..
Mellon, Secretary of the Treasury,
who had his tall young daughter. Miss
Eilsa Mellon, on his arm. The Secre.
tary of War and Mrs. Weeks, the
Secretary Of the Navy and Mrs. Den.
by, the Secretary of Commerce and
Mrs. Hoover, and the Secretary Of
Labor and Mrs. Davis were others In
this group.


The strains Of Hail to the Chief"
greeted the appearance Of the Chief
Executive, played by the Marine Band
under the direction of Lieutenant
Santelman. The band was stationed
in the main hallway, their scarlet
coats contributing a brilliant note Of
color. The Stars and Stripes, held
by soldiers in uniform, thanked the
doorway through which the Presi.
Dental party entered and gave a fur
ther touch of military pomp.

dent and Mrs. Harding took their
stand before the door leading into

NEW YORK.; May 23.-It will be
a long time before any "speakeasy"
bartender sympathizes again with a
well-dressed princess, even though
she intimates her earthly existence
In about to be cut short through
thirst.


At least a dozen proprietors, head
walters, and minor attaches OF cafes
in the theatrical district chorused
in court today an old, old resolution:


"Never again"


Their distress was due to the fact
that Bill. Jack, and Eddie were out
together last night with a nattily-
attired princess or rare Spanish
style and beauty. They drove a com.
manding.looking car with spare
parts and everything.


First, they posed as bookmakers.
The princess let a casual remark
drop about books. Bill STAFFORD,
Jack Kerrigan, and Eddie Potter
took UP the conversation like regu'
lar turf plungers.


Nicholas Diamond the head
waiter, was impressed.


The details of what next transpired
are old stuff.


After those formalities Nicholas
took a long running jump. He
landed in a dressing room full of
chorus girls. Confusion and con-
sternation, for thvy were innocent
little things. few over seventeen. and
none had ever spoken to a strange
man in their lives.


Mr.. Stafford followed. More
familiar formalities.


Then, with the thrill of living
coursing through their frames. Bill,
Jack, and Eddie and their princess
made the rounds.


Something inevitably happened in
each place. and some one always
got a ride.


Next they tried the exclusive
places. From an iron grating a
veiled face peered as the princess
pushed the bell


''Is Paul here?" she asked. The
words were magic. The door swung
open. The four walked in with their
heads high. When they came out
again the proprietor and head waiter
were on their way to the nearest
station.
